reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about phase transformations, deformation mechanisms, and a non-monotonic toughness trend in AlCoCrFeNi2.1, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the detailed ordering kinetics, boundary morphology evolution, or the proposed ductile–brittle–ductile transition in this specific alloy.
premises: Thermal aging induces L12 ordering in FCC domains of AlCoCrFeNi2.1
L12 ordering raises APBE and elastic modulus, restricting cross-slip and promoting planar slip
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries form during aging and act as stress concentrators
Embrittlement peaks at ~600°C due to maximum ordering and jagged boundary density
Ductility recovers at ~750°C because ordering diminishes and ductile transition zones form
